title: Rust: Vowel Counter
description: Count vowels (a, e, i, o, u) in a string.

steps.title: Count a Single Vowel
steps.description: Write a function `is_vowel(c: char) -> bool` that returns true if c is a vowel. Test with 'a' and 'b'.

steps.title: Count Vowels in a String
steps.description: Write a function `count_vowels(s: &str) -> u32` that counts all vowels. Call with `"hello world"` and print.
hints: Use the is_vowel function from step 1.

steps.title: Case-Insensitive Count
steps.description: Make is_vowel case-insensitive and count vowels in `"Hello World"`. Print the result.
hints: Or check both cases in is_vowel.
H e l l o   W o r l d → 3 vowels.

steps.title: Count Each Vowel Separately
steps.description: Write a function `count_each_vowel(s: &str)` that prints the count of each vowel (a, e, i, o, u) separately. Test with `"Rust is awesome!"`.
hints: Use a tuple or array of 5 counters.
Match each character against each vowel.
Rust is awesome! → a=0, e=2, i=1, o=1, u=1

verification.failureMessage: Print count of each vowel in 'Rust is awesome!'.

steps.title: Percentage of Vowels
steps.description: Write a function `vowel_percentage(s: &str) -> f64` that returns the percentage of vowels. Test with `"Rust programming"`.
hints: Percentage = (vowels as f64 / total as f64) * 100.0

verification.failureMessage: Print the vowel percentage of 'Rust programming'.
